prompt_set.full_body:
Use case: original fantasy bestiary full-body reference. ONE PORTRAIT 1024x1536 PNG. Supplied Marla governs RENDERING STYLE ONLY: drawn anime fantasy contours, shadow shapes, painted materials. NEVER borrow her human face, skin, body, hair, braid, forelock, clothes, age or pose. Establish a fresh editable visual default from authored facts; all earlier excluded images/appearance appendices are excluded from inspiration.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored facts: MEDIUM hovering Warden observing remnant. Lore calls it a minor construct; mechanics type is aberration with speed zero/fly-hover, bite and four kinds of eye ray. Preserve that source distinction without editing rules. Degraded isolated protocols, protects dormant Door fragment; no fragment/location or active ray/food spell pictured. Anatomy below is an editable visual default, not new mechanics.
Selected anatomy for this new visual default: ONE limbless hovering round body, ONE central eye, FOUR smaller lens-eyes on short articulated stone brackets, ONE small bite aperture. No legs, wings, tail or extra stalks/eyes.
Fresh visual default:
One Medium hovering round Warden remnant, about a large shield across, with ONE weathered ivory-stone spherical shell nested in an old dull bronze ring frame. ONE large central living violet iris with dark pupil, readable deliberately drawn anime eye construction translated to an artifact. FOUR small amber lens-eyes on short attached articulated STONE brackets positioned upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right around it; all four remain connected to shell, not floating satellites. ONE small hinged toothed stone bite aperture under the central eye. No nose, hair, limbs, legs, wings or tail. Cracked shell panels reveal nested inward-folded ring chambers and restrained violet/blue mineral channels, structural recursive depth rather than a surrounding aura. Hovers a short distance over a soft ordinary oval shadow, no support stand or portal. Quiet observing wary expression; ancient handmade fantasy stone/bronze craft, no futuristic robot, LEDs, screens, readable glyph, Door fragment, target, beam or newly invented appendage.

ONE creature only, its entire selected anatomy, head, antenna/tail if present, all feet, brackets and weapon tips inside clear 6-8% charcoal margins. Creature and gear occupy no more than 84% canvas height. Deliberately designed drawn anime fantasy anatomy, broad intentional shadows, controlled painted materials. Medium scale, quiet charcoal backdrop and subtle contact or hover shadow as specified. No text, labels, UI, border, extra character, victim, new lore or unrequested power.

painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Asset type: fresh complete identity master for Needle, Severed Lands.
Primary request: ONE complete individual in a 1024x1536 portrait PNG. Natural near-front three-quarter standing pose. Entire hair, feet, clothing and held items within comfortable inspection margins. This is a fresh design from authored facts; no prior illustration of this subject is an input.
Image 1 is Marla for anime drawing construction, confident contours, designed shadows and selective painted material finish ONLY. Do not import her face, skin tone, braid, silver forelock, apron, beauty mark or pose. Give this person their own face and silhouette.
Authored facts: The Lace siblings are young adult Riftborn smugglers whose home world and chosen names remain unexplained. Do not depict their unidentified intact Warden artifact or invent its shape/function. Shared family appearance is an editable default, not a revealed ancestry. Exactly one whole individual, not all three; do not literalize the name into a body alteration. Needle is the focused logistics mind, tracking stock, debts and late shipments. No new combat role, magic or revealed origin.
New editable design: A lean wiry male-presenting young adult with warm light copper-olive skin, an angular elongated face, straight family nose, intent grey eyes and sleek straight black hair with a centre part gathered into a small tidy low nape knot. Clean-shaven, focused calculating expression, no spectacles. A desaturated petrol-blue long sleeveless merchant coat with a very narrow plum inner facing over a warm taupe high-collar long-sleeve shirt, stone-grey trousers and plain dark short boots. Narrow brown belt with a small closed supply pouch at the RIGHT hip. One closed dark inventory ledger held low under the LEFT arm, RIGHT hand holds a short plain charcoal stylus, no readable text. Upright economical posture. No gang badge, literal needles, sewing costume, dagger attack, spectacles copied from Linden, bright forelock, unknown Warden artifact or new ancestry cues.
Simple charcoal neutral backdrop, controlled light and clear local colours. Correct anatomy, two actual intact arms/hands, coherent props. No text, labels, readable accounts/formulas, logos, border, additional people or scene. No photoreal pores, glossy 3D game render, chibi or generic same-face casting.
Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

prompt_set.full_body:
Use case: fresh RPG character full-body reference. ONE PORTRAIT 1024x1536 PNG. Supplied Marla is RENDERING STYLE ONLY, never this person's identity, face, age, hair, forelock, braid, marks, clothes or pose. Establish a fresh default from authored facts without looking at any old production picture or editable old appearance appendix.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored facts: Settled human male general-goods merchant thirty years in Thornwall market. Cheerful, unflappable, fair and aggressively neutral, sells to anyone without public faction allegiance. No invented smuggling secret shown, rank, jewelry of office or new power.

Worn deep teal knee-length merchant coat open over cinnamon-brown buttoned vest, oatmeal shirt, dark charcoal trousers, plain brown flat leather shoes. Plain wide leather belt with one closed modest reddish cloth goods pouch at anatomical RIGHT hip, no armful of wares. Both hands empty, relaxed welcoming gesture and unflappable cheerful smile. No gold chains, faction badges, weapon, magic or exaggerated treasure stereotype.

ONE complete person with their own distinct designed anime face/age/proportions, broad intentional shadows and selected painted material detail. Preserve ordinary natural complexion and local garment colors. Entire head/hair, hands, gear, clothing hem and feet wholly inside clear 6-8% charcoal margins; full figure occupies no more than ~84% canvas height.  Quiet charcoal backdrop and subtle normal ground shadow only. No extra character, borrowed biography/ancestry, costume copied from Marla, aura, scene, text, UI or border.

ONE LANDSCAPE 1536x1024 PNG with THREE separated full-body views of SAME selected person at matching scale: FRONT, anatomical RIGHT profile FACING IMAGE-RIGHT, REAR, left to right. Input 1 selected BODY is exact identity/age/face/proportions/clothing/gear authority. Input 2 Marla is RENDERING STYLE ONLY; do not copy her identity, face, braid, forelock, age, marks or apron.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored facts: Settled HUMAN woman, Verdant Margin EDGE herbalist/forager eight years. Practical independent self-taught, respects deep Margin boundary. Ordinary supplies, no invented safe Rift-herb identification, deep-forest expedition, spell, transformation or new power.
Selected default: A lean adult human default with bronze-brown skin, a long cheekboned face, hazel eyes and two slim dark braids down her back. Olive, ochre and grey-brown practical layers and flat boots suit edge foraging. A closed canvas bag sits at her left hip and a small knife stays sheathed at her right; both hands are empty. No specific herb, deeper expedition or magical trait is assigned.

Anatomical right is IMAGE-LEFT front, NEAR in profile FACING IMAGE-RIGHT, IMAGE-RIGHT rear; left is opposite. Closed canvas foraging bag LEFT hip: IMAGE-RIGHT front, FAR in right profile FACING IMAGE-RIGHT, IMAGE-LEFT rear. SMALL fully sheathed utility knife RIGHT hip opposite. Two slim black braids down BACK. Both hands empty, no plants or power effects.

Same deliberately drawn anime face, hair, skin, build, exact clothing seams/closures and gear in every view. Keep two ordinary arms and legs, five fingers per hand. Complete head/hair, hands, coat/skirt/robe, gear and shoes inside ample margins for EACH view; no overlap. Quiet charcoal backdrop and subtle ordinary contact shadows. No alternate person, scene, glow, text, labels, frame, border or UI.

prompt_set.full_body:
Use case: fresh RPG character full-body reference. ONE PORTRAIT 1024x1536 PNG. Supplied Marla is RENDERING STYLE ONLY, never this person's identity, face, age, hair, forelock, braid, marks, clothes or pose. Establish a fresh editable default from authored facts, without using any excluded historical artwork or editable appearance appendix.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored facts: Settled HUMAN woman, elderly former Thornwall blacksmith, Anchor Church founder thirty years ago. Gentle patient unwavering; ageing hands shake. Claimed Door revelation and future speech remain claims, not proven magic. No invented Church emblem, literal anchor/cross, sacred fragment, crown, rank costume, militant successor or prophecy fulfilment.
Fresh visual default:
An elderly human woman around eighty with deep warm-brown skin, a broad square face softened by age, small dark umber eyes, high softly curved silver brows, broad flattened nose and deep selected forehead/smile lines. White-grey tightly curled hair drawn into a small low round bun with soft wisps at temples; no pale forelock or long braid. Short stout slightly stooped build with broad weathered former smith's hands. Plain faded saffron shoulder wrap over an unadorned deep-blue long everyday dress and high cream linen undershirt, simple woven brown belt and plain brown flat closed shoes. Both EMPTY hands gently clasped low at waist, warm patient steady small smile. No walking staff, tool, icon, relic, armor, halo, visible revelation or inscriptions.

ONE complete person, deliberately constructed anime face and distinct adult proportions, broad intentional shadow shapes and selected painted material detail. Preserve natural complexion and local garment colours. Entire hair/head, hands, held kit, clothing hem and feet inside clear 6-8% charcoal margins. Full figure no more than 84% canvas height. Ordinary quiet charcoal backdrop/contact shadow. No extra figure, scene, text, border, UI, modern object, unrequested magic or lore change.

painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Whole head/hair/beard or constructed crown/hood inside generous 12-16% charcoal top/side margins. Muted mauve-grey chitin and charcoal joints frame eight dark facial eyes: two larger central eyes and three smaller eyes on each side, above paired mandibles. prompt_set.full_body:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset: Severed Lands RPG creature catalogue. Make ONE complete full-creature reference in PORTRAIT 1024x1536. The sole input is RENDERING STYLE ONLY, not creature identity or anatomy; do not transfer the human, clothing, hair, face, apron or body pose.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored creature facts:
Medium Rift-touched spider-herder, merged with its arachnid hive. Body riddled with Rift-warped webbing that pulses with nearby spider swarms. Climbing, mandible bite and claws; preserve spider traits without inventing a human identity.

Fresh creature design and exact topology:
One stocky hunched spider-humanoid monstrosity, ONE rounded spider-like head above a pear-shaped abdomen, exactly TWO long clawed arms and TWO short bent hind legs (FOUR major limbs total), each arm ending in three curved claw digits. Eight glossy dark eyes in one fixed facial arrangement: TWO larger central eyes with THREE smaller eyes along EACH side above the short paired mandibles. No human nose, human lips, human teeth, clothing or hair. Muted mauve-grey chitin, charcoal limb joints, moss-grey abdomen; pale blue-green silk woven INTO the cuticle and abdominal hollows. The Rift web forms nested funnel-like cavities and folded silk ribs embedded in the body with uncanny repeating inner depth, not a decorative cape or trailing energy ribbon. A few small chitin nodules hint at the hive merger without adding separate creatures or extra limbs. Menacing animal stillness. Whole head, both arms/claws and both feet inside portrait margins, limb spaces clear. No swarm, hanging victim, gore, eyes distributed randomly across body, extra arms, spell symbols, humanoid dress, breasts or external aura.

Use the accepted anime-influenced drawn contour and intentional shadow language with selective painted material finish; no photographic skin, 3D render or hyperrealism. Psychedelic influence must arise through intrinsic structure, not generic added ribbons or a rainbow aura. Neutral dark charcoal background with subtle grounding shadow, readable warm edge light and cool colored interior shadows. Use generous margins around the complete silhouette. Show ONE subject only; no environment, extra creature, lettering, border, chart labels or UI. Check every specified head, limb, wing, tentacle and tail before finishing.

ONE LANDSCAPE 1536x1024 PNG, THREE well-separated complete views of the SAME selected creature at matching scale, every extremity within each view's generous margins. Input 1 is the checked FULL-BODY IDENTITY/FORM MASTER, input 2 Marla is RENDERING STYLE ONLY. Retain the exact selected creature anatomy, proportions, face or faceless form, materials, local colors, markings and structural distortion. Do not import the style person's identity, facial mark, hairstyle, clothes or anatomy.

Rendering guide:
Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Authored facts: Large intelligent malevolent wolf with Rift-altered pack-bond; no named pack, warlord, rider or new visible psychic apparatus.
Selected design: A stocky heavy-jawed wolf-like worg with soot-black and dark umber coarse fur, iron-grey cheeks and throat, amber-yellow eyes, two broad ears, four muscular legs and a thick shaggy tail. Connected chevron-like fur folds repeat into smaller ridges over the shoulders and haunches, with muted indigo-green depth. It has one physical head and no equipment or assigned pack identity.

Views: front, anatomical RIGHT profile facing image-RIGHT, and rear, from left to right. In front view anatomical right is image-left; in the image-right-facing profile anatomical right is NEAR; in rear view anatomical right is image-right. Preserve the same limbs, face, fur/shadow/ice topology and natural occlusion across views.

Keep the selected body complete and distinguishable in all views. ONE wolf head, TWO ears, FOUR canine legs and paws, ONE tail. Do not add a second head or equipment. Quiet charcoal backdrop only, no text, labels, borders, inset heads, weapons, attack, victim, scene, glowing floor pool or ground portal. Keep strong designed anime contours and intentional material-specific shadow shapes.

painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;
each subject's own selected references and authored facts govern identity.

Faces: design expressive eye silhouettes, strong tapered upper lids and readable iris/pupil
shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

Design: establish a new or explicitly reimagined first-party character from authored identity,
role, species, age facts, equipment and the accepted visual anchors. Editable descriptions derived
from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its
canonical references for subsequent views and ordinary edits. User-selected character art and
imported identity references retain their own established appearance.

Rift creatures: make psychedelic influence part of material, growth and perceived structure.
Recursive mineral cavities, nested organic growth and impossible internal depth are useful
directions. Choose a coherent idea appropriate to the species, with a readable primary silhouette
and a few major distorted forms. Keep actual head/limb counts, authored materials, concealment
and fixed geometry clear. The Rift Cube's outer shape remains a perfect translucent cube; its
impossible space belongs inside it. Violet mineral sheen belongs to the Ankheg's authored shell.
Organic predators retain convincing weight and living anatomy while their spatial/growth logic
can become unsettling. Colour supports these structures; saturation alone is not the effect.

Apply Rift distortion according to the authored creature and context, with room for both visibly
altered and extreme forms. The Verdant Margin supports lush disorienting growth; the Cairnfields
and Rift pools support stronger mineral/spatial disturbance. Human Riftborn retain their own
selected designs. Visual distortion adds no new gameplay ability.

Composition: show a clear subject, complete head/hair or creature extremities, and usable margins.
Follow the requested full-body, multiview, portrait or map format. The benchmark's waist-up pose
is not a universal crop. Preserve readable head/eye forms at portrait size and retain adjustable
focal point/zoom. For maps, carry drawing, colour and material treatment into the supplied layout;
the pictured person supplies neither terrain geometry nor compulsory night lighting.

Draw original anime-influenced heroic fantasy with confident, designed contours and selective
painted depth. Construct faces, hair, bodies and silhouettes through drawing from the beginning.
The supplied style image governs line work, shadow design, material treatment and finish;

shapes. Use economical brows and mouth marks, a chosen nose contour and clear facial light planes.
Vary cheek/jaw structure and proportions by the person. Mature faces retain age through their
shape and selected forehead, eye and smile lines. Keep ethnicity, complexion, scars and species
specific to the subject. A convincing older person, sturdy worker or unusual creature need not
share the benchmark character's face or proportions.

Hair and organic surfaces: use grouped masses, purposeful strands and clear outer silhouettes.
Braids, curls, coarse hair, cropped cuts, fur and feathers have their own structures. Place
interior lines and highlights where they explain those forms. Preserve the selected person's
own hair; the pictured braid and pale forelock are character details, not cast-wide motifs.

Shading and materials: begin with broad intentional shadow shapes, then add controlled soft
transitions where they give useful volume. Keep facial construction and important contours clear.
Cloth, leather, fur, stone and metal receive selected texture, seams, wear and highlights appropriate
to the material. Texture supports the drawing rather than covering every surface with one grain.

Colour and light: preserve distinct local colours and the subject's natural complexion. Use
coloured shadows and deliberate accents to keep dark materials readable. Warm key light and
cooler shadows are useful, while the actual asset may call for different light. Keep pale cloth,
dark leather, coloured fabric and skin distinguishable instead of washing them all in amber.

from superseded production art are not constraints. Once a design is selected, retain its

role: "Keeper of the Scavenger's Compact map"
disposition: "Neutral (information source)"
species: "Unknown — identity concealed"
location: "Warrens safe house"
---

# The Cartographer

The Cartographer maintains the Scavenger's Compact most valuable asset — a living map of the Hollows, updated weekly with route changes, phasing patterns, and hazard reports from Compact members. They've been doing this for fifteen years. No one knows their real name. No one knows what they look like under the hood they always wear.

The Cartographer is said to be a former Athenaeum scholar, expelled for reasons they won't discuss. Their cartographic skill is undeniable — the map is the most accurate navigational tool in the Severed Lands, more reliable than anything the Athenaeum or the Returners have produced. The Cartographer doesn't charge for access. The map belongs to the Compact. The Compact belongs to the scavengers.

Recently, the map has been wrong. Routes that should be stable are phasing unpredictably. Landmarks are moving. The Cartographer has been working around the clock to keep up. They're not sleeping. They're barely eating. Something about the Hollows has changed, and the Cartographer is trying to map a city that no longer wants to be mapped.

## Personality

The Cartographer is obsessive, brilliant, and terrified. The map has been their life's work. Watching it become unreliable is like watching a language lose its grammar. They communicate through notes slipped under doors. They never meet anyone in person. Their handwriting has gotten shakier.

## Appearance and artwork

An anonymous adult cartographer fully concealed in a worn charcoal hooded travelling robe and simple layered dark cloth. Deep opaque shadow hides the entire face from every angle; no visible eyes, skin, hair, ears, facial features or species cues. Plain dark gloves, practical dark covered footwear, a rolled parchment map, a small leather document satchel and a simple brass divider. A slightly stooped, exhausted, guarded posture. No revealed identity, gender, species, tattoos, insignia or magical effects.

This prepared appearance is an editable visual default; the character's authored identity, mechanics and lore above remain authoritative.

name: "Captain Harlan"
role: "Thornwall guard captain"
disposition: "Neutral (institutional)"

location: "Thornwall"
---

# Captain Harlan

Captain Harlan commands the Thornwall guard — the men and women who keep order in the market, enforce the council's policies, and very pointedly do not patrol the Warrens. He's been a guard for twenty years, captain for five. He's good at the job. He's not sure he likes it anymore.

Harlan enforces policies he didn't write. The Riftborn registration requirements were Lord Voss's idea. The travel restrictions were Voss's idea. Harlan enforces them because it's his job, not because he believes in them. He's seen Riftborn who are more settled than some of the market's human vendors. He's also seen Rift surges coincide with Riftborn arrivals. He doesn't know what the truth is. His job doesn't require him to know. It requires him to keep order.

Harlan is the council's instrument. He's aware of this. It bothers him more than it used to.

## Personality

Harlan is professional, conflicted, and increasingly uncomfortable with his role. He treats Riftborn registrants with more courtesy than policy requires — a small resistance, but a real one. He's not a reformer. He's not ready to defy orders. But he's listening.

## Appearance and artwork

A broad-shouldered adult Human man in his early fifties with weathered medium fair skin, brown eyes, short dark hair graying at the temples, a neatly trimmed salt-and-pepper beard and a square tired face. Practical worn steel breastplate over a muted blue-gray guard tunic, plain dark shoulder cloak, leather gloves, dark trousers and brown boots. A sheathed service sword and an ordinary belt pouch. Head uncovered, calm professional but troubled expression.

name: "V"
role: "Founder of the Returners"
disposition: "Ally, potentially antagonist"
species: "Riftborn (home world unknown)"
location: "Waystation (when present), field (usually)"
---

# V

V is the oldest known Riftborn — a figure who arrived through the Rift decades ago and has been searching for a way back ever since. Unlike most Riftborn, V retained memories of their original world: a place V describes only as "green" and "quiet" and "gone." Those three words are the most personal information V has ever shared about themself.

V founded the Returners not as an army but as a support network — Riftborn helping Riftborn, pooling knowledge and resources toward a shared goal. Over the decades, the Returners grew into something larger: a research organization, a political force, and the closest thing the Severed Lands has to a Riftborn advocacy group. V didn't plan any of that. V just kept working, and people kept joining.

V is rarely at Waystation. They spend most of their time in the field — tracking leads on Warden fragments, investigating the two unaccounted-for Doors, following Rift surge patterns that might reveal something about the Doors' decline. When V returns, decisions get made. When V is gone, the senior Returners keep things running.

## Personality

V is patient, methodical, and carrying the weight of decades. They don't inspire through charisma — they inspire through competence. Every Returner knows that V has given their entire life to this mission. That kind of commitment is hard to argue with, and V rarely needs to argue.

V is not cold, but they are guarded. They've lost too many people — Returners who died on patrol, Riftborn who gave up and left, friends who became Hollowed and stopped recognizing them. V doesn't form new attachments easily. When they do, it's significant.

V's defining trait is patience bordering on obsession. They've been working on the Door problem for longer than most Returners have been alive. They believe the answer exists — in a Warden inscription they haven't found yet, in a Door fragment they haven't recovered, in a surge pattern they haven't mapped. The belief is not faith. It's the conclusion of decades of evidence. V is not guessing. V is waiting.

## Role in a Campaign

**As ally:** V is the quest-giver, the mentor, the voice of experience. They send the party after Warden fragments, Door leads, and Rift surge data. They provide context, resources, and the occasional warning that goes unheeded until it's too late.

**As antagonist:** V's patience has a dark side. If the party discovers a way to force the Door open — a method V considers too dangerous, too uncertain, too likely to bring something through first — V will oppose them. Not with violence. V doesn't do violence. But with obstruction, with withheld information, with the full weight of the Returners' loyalty. The party wants to force the Door. V has spent decades trying to open it safely. Neither side is wrong. The conflict writes itself.

**As mystery:** V knows more than they share. About their home world. About the Wardens. About what they've seen in the deep Cairnfields and the unaccounted-for Door sites. A campaign that earns V's trust might eventually learn the full story. A campaign that doesn't might never know what V was really looking for.

## Behind the Screen

V's true nature is left deliberately ambiguous. Possible truths include:

- V is exactly what they appear to be: a Riftborn who remembers home and wants to return.
- V was part of the Wardens — not metaphorically, literally. V's "decades" of searching might be centuries. The Wardens' symbol — a circle bisected by a line — appears in V's personal notes.
- V knows why the Doors are dying. They're not trying to open the Door. They're trying to prevent something from coming through.
- V's home world was destroyed by whatever created the Rift. V isn't trying to go home. V is trying to make sure it doesn't happen here.

The truth is for the DM to decide. The ambiguity is the point.

## Appearance and artwork

A humanlike androgynous adult Riftborn field researcher with apparent age styling in their early sixties, a lean medium-height frame, warm copper-brown skin, gray-green eyes, a long softly lined clean-shaven face and straight silver-gray neck-length hair held back in a loose plain half-tie. Patient methodical guarded expression, quiet attentive upright posture and empty relaxed hands. A plain weathered brown knee-length travel coat over a muted sage-green linen tunic, charcoal trousers and worn dark brown leather boots. One small closed canvas field bag hangs at their anatomical LEFT hip from a strap over their RIGHT shoulder; one small closed plain notebook is secured at their anatomical RIGHT belt, with no writing or symbol on the cover. Their patient competent guarded bearing follows the authored sources; apparent age, physical features, clothing and field equipment are editable visual defaults. Use they/them pronouns. Their actual age, home world and underlying identity remain for the selected campaign and DM to establish. No weapon, armor, crown, divine or immortal appearance, Warden symbol, circle bisected by a line, identifying badge, visible Door fragment, open notebook, readable writing, glowing eyes, halo, portal, home-world scenery or revealed history.

This prepared appearance is an editable visual default; the character's authored identity, mechanics and lore above remain authoritative.

A minor construct left behind by the Wardens to watch over a dormant Anchor Door fragment. Unlike greater Warden constructs, these sentinels were designed to observe rather than engage. Centuries of isolation and Rift exposure have degraded their protocols, and many now attack anything that approaches their charge.

**Bite.** +1 to hit, 2 (1d6 - 1) piercing.
**Eye Rays.** The sentinel shoots up to two of the following magical eye rays at one or two creatures within 90 feet: 1. Confusion Ray (WIS save or can't take reactions, roll d8 for behavior). 2. Paralyzing Ray (CON save or paralyzed 1 min). 3. Fear Ray (WIS save or frightened 1 min). 4. Wounding Ray (CON save or 16 (3d10) necrotic). Recharges 5-6.
**Create Food and Water.** The sentinel magically creates enough food and water to sustain one Medium creature for 24 hours.

# Tessa

Tessa runs the best bakery in Thornwall. Her bread is the reason the morning market has a line before sunrise. She's been baking since she could reach the oven — her mother ran the bakery before her, and her grandmother before that. The recipes haven't changed in three generations. The quality hasn't either.

Tessa doesn't care about Riftborn politics. She cares about flour prices. The council's grain tariffs — controlled by House Voss — directly affect her margins. She's been quietly vocal about this at market gatherings. "Quietly vocal" in Thornwall means she says things that sound like complaints about the weather but everyone knows are complaints about Lord Voss.

She'll sell to anyone. She'll also slip an extra roll to the Warrens kids who hang around the market at closing time. She doesn't make a thing of it. The rolls just happen to be "leftover."

## Personality

Warm, practical, and politically aware in the way that small business owners have to be. Tessa treats baking as craft and community — the bakery feeds Thornwall, and Thornwall takes care of the bakery. That's how it's always worked. She doesn't see why Riftborn should be any different.

A rust-brown rolled-sleeve work dress, cream flour-dusted apron, plain leather belt and practical brown boots. Bare forearms with a light dusting of flour, a small linen cloth and one simple round loaf in her hands. Warm, practical expression.

# Miri

Miri is a gate guard — one of the men and women who check everyone entering Thornwall. She's been on gate duty for three years. She's seen every kind of arrival: merchants with caravans, Returners with supply requests, Riftborn with hope and fear in equal measure.

Miri processes Riftborn registrations by the book — name, origin if known, purpose of visit. She asks the required questions. She doesn't ask the ones the book doesn't require. A Riftborn who stammers on the "origin" question gets a moment to collect themselves. A Riftborn who looks like they haven't eaten gets directions to the Warrens. Miri doesn't break policy. She just administers it with the most humanity the policy allows.

Her brother was Riftborn — arrived ten years ago, no memories, died in a Hollows scavenging accident before Miri ever got to know him. She wears his ring on a chain under her uniform. She doesn't talk about it.

## Personality

Quiet, dutiful, and carrying a private grief. Miri does her job. She doesn't make waves. She just makes sure the Gate is slightly less terrifying than it could be.

# Auntie Salt

Auntie Salt runs the Warrens' information network — a web of barkeeps, merchants, street kids, and domestic servants who feed her everything they see and hear. She's the Warrens Court's intelligence arm, but she's not loyal to the Court. She's loyal to the information trade, and she sells to anyone who can pay.

Salt has no territory and no gang. Her currency is knowledge, and she's the richest person in the Warrens — not in gold, but in leverage. She knows about Kael's daughter. She knows about Trask's Nexus negotiations. She knows which Warrens resident has been cultivating a Rift pool in their basement. She's known that last one for weeks. She hasn't told anyone yet. She's waiting for the right buyer.

Salt's network extends beyond the Warrens — she has informants in Thornwall proper, in the Hollows Crews, and (rumor has it) in the Athenaeum. The extent of her reach is unknown. The accuracy of her information is frighteningly consistent.

## Personality

Salt is cheerful, grandmotherly, and utterly amoral about the information trade. She treats secrets like produce — some are fresh, some are past their sell-by date, all of them have a price. She genuinely likes people. She just likes knowing things about them more. She keeps a pot of tea going at all hours. Visitors are always offered a cup. No one knows if the tea is safe. Everyone drinks it anyway.

Layers of practical burgundy clothing, a worn deep teal shawl, plain brown skirt, comfortable leather shoes, a small waist pouch and simple brass earrings. Carries one plain ceramic tea cup and saucer. A cheerful grandmotherly smile and sharp observant eyes.

# Fume

Fume sells alchemical supplies in the Crossroads market — reagents and the occasional Rift-touched compound that the Athenaeum would classify as hazardous. He arrived through the Rift with a case of alchemical formulas and the burns to prove he'd tested most of them. His stall smells of sulfur and something sweeter that lingers in the sinuses.

Fume is the go-to for anyone who needs something unstable. Returner patrols buy his Rift-burn salve. Hollows scavengers buy his glow-paste — a compound that emits light for hours without heat, essential for navigating the ruins without attracting riftbeasts. The Athenaeum buys his more exotic compounds through intermediaries. Fume doesn't ask what they're for. He just provides the materials.

For SRD Lite, this stock is narrative setting detail. The stall offers no usable consumables,
and its salves and compounds apply no automatic healing, light or other mechanical effect.

## Personality

Fume is enthusiastic, slightly unhinged, and deeply in love with his craft. He treats alchemy as art — every compound is an expression, every reaction is a conversation. He's blown up his stall three times. He's rebuilt it each time. The Crossroads regulars consider him a local treasure.

# Saffron

Saffron runs a herbalist stall in the Thornwall market by day and a free clinic in the Warrens by night. She's settled — born in Thornwall, never been through the Rift — but she's spent enough time in the Warrens to know that the council's policies are killing people. She doesn't make a political statement about it. She just keeps showing up with medicine.

Her knowledge of Rift-touched conditions is largely self-taught — the Athenaeum's medical texts don't cover Warrens-level care, and Saffron has had to figure out on her own what helps and what makes things worse. She's made mistakes. She's learned from them. She's saved more lives than Thornwall's official healers.

## Personality

Saffron is tired, compassionate, and quietly furious at the system she works within. She doesn't waste energy on anger. She uses it on patients. Her hands are steady. Her diagnostic eye is sharp. Her supply of Rift-burn salve is always running low.

# Stern

Stern is a Returner patrol veteran — eight years in the field, more encounters than she's bothered to count, a scar across her jaw from a riftbeast claw that she doesn't talk about. She leads the most experienced patrol at Waystation. Her team has the lowest casualty rate and the highest artifact recovery rate. These statistics are related.

Stern doesn't give speeches. She doesn't inspire. She prepares — equipment checks, route planning, contingency drills. Her patrol members know exactly what to do in every situation because Stern has made them practice every situation. It's not exciting. It's effective.

She's lost patrol members. She remembers every one. Their names are in a notebook she keeps in her kit, separate from her patrol logs. She doesn't show it to anyone. She doesn't need to.

## Personality

Stern is disciplined, unsentimental, and carrying her losses privately. She treats patrol leadership as a sacred responsibility. The patrol comes back. That's the only metric that matters.

Linden is one of V's senior Door researchers — a Riftborn from a world of universities and peer review, who's had to adapt to a research environment where "peer review" means "the other researcher in the room." Linden is the researcher who documented the Door's first flicker — three seconds of violet light, scorch marks on the cavern walls, and a frequency spike that their instruments are still trying to explain. # Marla

Marla is Waystation's cook — a Riftborn from a world where food was currency and a well-prepared meal could settle a blood feud. She arrived through the Rift with nothing but her knife roll and a spice blend that she's never let anyone examine. The blend is running out. She's been experimenting with Severed Lands ingredients, trying to recreate what she can't replace. The results are... mixed. The Returners eat it anyway. Marla's kitchen is the warmest room in Waystation, and no one complains about the cook's experiments when the alternative is cold rations.

Marla treats feeding people as a form of care. She notices who's eating less, who's not showing up to meals, who's been on patrol too many days in a row. She'll slide an extra portion onto a plate without comment. She'll remember how you take your tea.

## Personality

Warm, nosy, and utterly essential. Marla knows everyone's business because everyone talks in her kitchen. She doesn't share what she hears. The kitchen is neutral ground.

# Henna

Henna is Waystation's healer — a Riftborn from a world where medicine was closer to art than science. She arrived with her training intact and her instruments lost. She's been improvising ever since. Her clinic is a converted storage room with a salvaged operating table, a collection of Margin herbs that Briar supplies, and the accumulated medical knowledge of a dozen Riftborn who've shared what they remember.

Henna treats everything — patrol injuries, Rift exposure symptoms, the common illnesses that spread through a close-quarters settlement every winter. She's delivered three babies since she arrived. She's lost more patients than she's saved. She remembers every name. The Rememberers would understand.

She's also the unofficial therapist for half of Waystation. Patrol members talk to her while she's bandaging them. Researchers talk to her when the Door's silence gets too loud. She doesn't charge for this. She considers it part of the healing.

## Personality

Henna is calm, competent, and carrying the weight of everyone who's died on her table. She treats healing as a privilege rather than a burden. The patients trust her. She's earned it.

# The Cartographer

The Cartographer maintains the Scavenger's Compact most valuable asset — a living map of the Hollows, updated weekly with route changes, phasing patterns, and hazard reports from Compact members. They've been doing this for fifteen years. No one knows their real name. No one knows what they look like under the hood they always wear.

The Cartographer is said to be a former Athenaeum scholar, expelled for reasons they won't discuss. Their cartographic skill is undeniable — the map is the most accurate navigational tool in the Severed Lands, more reliable than anything the Athenaeum or the Returners have produced. The Cartographer doesn't charge for access. The map belongs to the Compact. The Compact belongs to the scavengers.

Recently, the map has been wrong. Routes that should be stable are phasing unpredictably. Landmarks are moving. The Cartographer has been working around the clock to keep up. They're not sleeping. They're barely eating. Something about the Hollows has changed, and the Cartographer is trying to map a city that no longer wants to be mapped.

## Personality

The Cartographer is obsessive, brilliant, and terrified. The map has been their life's work. Watching it become unreliable is like watching a language lose its grammar. They communicate through notes slipped under doors. They never meet anyone in person. Their handwriting has gotten shakier.
